Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- Ravindra Singh,Dinesh Rai,Kuldeep Singh Chahar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate
Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Heard learned counsel for the revisionist and learned Aga for the State.

The present revision is directed against the order dated 30.03.1999 passed by Additional Session Judge, Tenth, Agra in Criminal Appeal No.2 of 1998 (Bhudeo Vs. State) and the order dated 08.12.1997 in Case No.3315 of 1994 (Food Inspector Vs. Bhudeo).

sentences.text: The allegations against the revisionist are of adulteration of milk based on the report of the Public Analyst wherein it is noted that the fat content in the sample of cow milk was found less than the standard.

As per the standard,
fat content in the milk ought to be 3.5, whereas it was found 2.9 in the milk sample collected on 31.03.1988.
The revisionist was nabbed by the Food Inspector while he was going on cycle with the container to sell the milk.

The submission of learned counsel for the revisionist is that the sample collected from the revisionist was not found adulterated with any hazardous substance and further on account of delay caused in getting the Public Analyst report, opportunity of the revisionist under Section 13 (2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act' 1954 has been taken away.
Bhudeo vs State Of U.P. on 18 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152140553/
1
As per the said provision, the revisionist is entitled to get the sample analysed by the Central Food Laboratory, i.e. to get an independent analysis to contradict the Pubic Analyst report.
There is inordinate delay in registration of the complaint and receipt of the Public Analyst report.

Having gone through the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the records, it is more than evident that the conviction of the revisionist based on the Public Analyst report cannot be sustained as he did not get a fair and impartial trial in the case lodged against him.

Having gone through the judgements of the courts below, it is evident that there is no discussion in the order of conviction with regard to the service of public analyst report to the accused within time prescribed under Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act.

The Apex Court in the case of Vijendra vs. State of UP reported in AIR 2019 SC 4351 has held that the requirement of Section 13(2) of the Food and Adulteration Act to send the report after institution of prosecution against the person within time prescribed under Rule 9B of Rules, 1955 is mandatory and substantial compliance of the said provision is needed to sustain the conviction.

entities.text: Vijendra vs. State of UP reported in AIR 2019 SC 4351
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A valuable right has been given to an accused to get an independent Analyst report under Rule 9B of the Rules, 1955 that Local (Health) Authority shall send the report based on which action is taken,
within ten days after institution of the prosecution.
Sending such a report by registered post would not be substantial compliance of Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954.
The very purpose of furnishing such report is to enable the accused to seek for reference to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis, if he dissatisfied with the report.
Such safeguard provided to the accused under Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954 is valuable right.
In case, the report is send beyond the period prescribed under Rule 9B, the valuable right available to the accused to seek for independent analysis or reference stands defeated.
Since the accused is made to suffer penal consequences of prosecution, the provisions of Section 13(2) read with Rule 9(B) of Rules, 1955 have to be construed strictly.

In the light of the legal position noted above, in the instant case, it is found that the public analyst report was not sent nor it was proved that the said report was served on the accused/revisionist within 10 days of the lodging of the prosecution.
The revisionist, thus, did not get opportunity to analyse the sample through an independent analyst i.e. the Central Laboratory.

Further, it is also noteworthy that there was considerable delay in launching prosecution, in as much as, sample was taken on 31.03.1988 and after six months of receipt of the public analyst report, sanction for prosecution was given and the complaint was filed on 30.09.1988.

Even if, it is accepted for a moment that the public analyst report was sent through registered post to the accused-revisionist was received by him, there was considerable delay in sending the same,
which has resulted in frustration of the right given to the accused-revisionist under Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954.
The reason being that it would not be possible to retain the same properties of milk for a period of approximately ten months.
The properties of the milk sample was bound to change during such a long period taken in launching prosecution and furnishing public analyst report to the revisionist.

It was, therefore, not possible for the accused/revisionist to get correct analysis of the Bhudeo vs State Of U.P. on 18 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152140553/
2 milk sample.
From all angles, the conviction of the revisionist being in violation of the statutory provisions cannot be sustained.

Both the orders dated 30.03.1999 passed by Additional Session Judge, Tenth, Agra in Criminal Appeal No.2 of 1998 (Bhudeo Vs. State) and the order dated 08.12.1997 passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate (I), Agra in Case No.3315 of 1994 (Food Inspector Vs. Bhudeo) are hereby set aside.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The criminal revision is allowed.
The revisionist is acquitted of the charges under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The bail bonds furnished by the revisionist are discharged.
Fine, if paid, be refunded to the revisionist.
The revision is allowed.
Certify the judgment to the court below immediately.
